title: stepscroll tiles
description: Every tile a page of the world can hold, keyed by the tile's name. A page is 256 pixels across and 256 lines down. A tile's pieces, in Cyberun's form (examples/jetrun/world/tiles.schema.json), decide where the rock is: rock and sky by parity down each world column, sky above the world, turned by every floor or ceiling crossed. A tile may take another's pieces, mirrored or upside down, Cyberun's way. Its entries are what is drawn over that: graphics from steps.json. See world.py.

entries.description: What the display list draws in this page: graphics from steps.json, drawn exactly as they are, over the rock the pieces decide.

from.description: The tile whose pieces this one draws.

mirrored.description: Its source's pieces drawn mirrored left to right, Cyberun's $FF marker (for the rock; the tile's own entries are drawn as they are).

upsideDown.description: Its source's pieces drawn upside down, Cyberun's $99 marker (for the rock; the tile's own entries are drawn as they are).

entries.description: What the display list draws in this page: graphics from steps.json, drawn exactly as they are, over the rock the pieces decide.

x.description: The left edge of the piece's lowest step, in pixels from the page's left edge (a multiple of 8).

y.description: The bottom line of the piece's lowest step in the page: odd, as the blitters go up a row pair at a time.

direction.description: Cyberun's sixteen: flat steps 24 pixels long, gentle slopes 16 across and 8 up, plain ones 8 and 8, steep ones 8 and 16, walls 16 high. Floors have rock below, ceilings rock above; 'up' climbs to the right, 'down' climbs to the left.

column.description: The byte column of its left byte in the page, 0 to 31.

bottom.description: Its bottom line in the page: odd, as the blitters go up a row pair at a time.
